newsitem.title: USA: "The Nutcracker" is White House Christmas theme.
newsitem.headline: "The Nutcracker" is White House Christmas theme.

text.p: With violinists playing Christmas carols in the background, first lady Hillary Rodham Clinton Monday unveiled "The Nutcracker" ballet as this year's White House holiday theme.

Clinton, standing in the East Room that holds the towering 18 1/2 foot Colorado blue spruce that serves as the official White House Christmas tree, said the ballet classic has been a long-time favourite of the first family.
She said the ballet was "particularly special" to her, President Clinton and their 16-year-old daughter Chelsea ever since they took Chelsea to her first performance when she was two years old.

Chelsea, who studies ballet at a school in Washington, has performed various roles in the ballet every year since she was three, the first lady said. She added that her daughter will play four different roles this holiday season in select shows.

The White House tree is adorned with about 750 ornaments depicting scenes from the ballet like toy soldiers, nutcrackers, the Sugar Plum Fairy and the battle between the dolls and mice. It is illuminated by 5,040 lights.

The tree skirt consists of individual quilted panels representing the 50 states, territories and the District of Columbia and has been used under their tree every year since their first White House Christmas in 1993, Clinton said.

Throughout the presidential mansion the theme of "The Nutcracker" is apparent. The traditional gingerbread house in the State Dining Room depicts a Victorian-era home where two nutcracker soldiers stand guard outside. It is made of 60 pounds of gingerbread and took three White House pastry chefs nearly five months to make.
The first lady also unveiled the Clintons' Christmas card, which this year featured a reproduction of American artist Thomas McKnight's painting titled "White House Green Room."
The card, which shows stockings for the president, first lady and their daughter hung on the mantel, is to be sent to about 300,000 families, the White House said.
